copy.blurb:
The model fancies Ecuador more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Germany. +13.6pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

On Elo, Germany comes in 110 points ahead — Ecuador at 1790, Germany at 1900. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 27%, the draw at 23%, and Germany to win at 50%. The home side reads 27% on this distribution — the model's central case for Ecuador.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Ecuador to win at 13%, the draw at 22%, and Germany to win at 62%. The Ecuador side trades at 13% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +669. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 27%, +13.6pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Ecuador, that haircut lands the model at 23%; the market is at 13%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +9.5pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 35 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
